title: The ALMA survey to Resolve exoKuiper belt Substructures (ARKS): VIII. A dust arc and non-Keplerian gas kinematics in HD 121617
question: Characterise the dust arc, the dust and CO gas distributions, and the gas kinematics (non-Keplerian rotation) of the gas-rich exoKuiper belt HD 121617, to constrain the arc origin and the gas origin

data.sensitivity: peak S/N of ALMA dust, 12CO and 13CO images: 24, 21, 19

what.value: SPHERE scattered-light image, originally presented in Perrot2023 and re-reduced in ARKS

evidence.quote: The data were originally presented in (cite: Perrot2023) and re-reduced by (cite: scat_arks) as part of ARKS.

what.value: Stellar mass 1.90 +/- 0.01 Msun from stellar evolution models

evidence.quote: These values are well in agreement with the $1.90\pm0.01\ M_{\odot}$ inferred using stellar evolution models (cite: overview_arks).

evidence.quote: We assume that $\beta=-0.14$, $T_{0}=38$ K, and $r_0$=73 au as found in (cite: line_arks) by fitting the $^{13}$CO data cube.

recipe.goal: Extract radial and azimuthal profiles of dust, CO and scattered light
recipe.method: Radial and azimuthal intensity profiles from the SPHERE image, ARKS continuum and 12CO/13CO moment 0 images, using wedges for radial profiles and an averaged annulus for azimuthal profiles
key_parameters: ALMA radial profiles: two opposing 120 deg wide wedges along the major axis (SPHERE: 60 deg wedges)
Azimuthal profiles averaged over 65-90 au with a rolling azimuthal window of 40 deg
assumptions: Images are well centred on the stars (stellar location uncertainty <~10 mas for ALMA)

recipe.goal: Fit an axisymmetric plus arc model to the continuum visibilities
recipe.method: Parametric disc2radmc density model, radiative-transfer image, Fourier transform and likelihood with Galario, MCMC sampling
key_parameters: Axisymmetric component: double power law fitted to the azimuthally averaged radial profile
Arc component: 2D Gaussian in r and azimuth, with separate azimuthal widths on the leading and trailing sides
Free parameters also include inclination, position angle, and RA/Dec offsets
assumptions: Dust size distribution 1 um to 1 cm, exponent -3.5
Composition 70% astrosilicates, 15% crystalline water ice, 15% amorphous carbon by mass

recipe.goal: Fit a Keplerian model to the 12CO line-of-sight velocity map
recipe.method: Gaussian-method moment 1 map with BETTERMOMENTS from the robust 0.5 cube, then Keplerian fit with EDDY for orientation, systemic velocity and stellar mass
assumptions: Emission arises from the midplane (elevated-surface models gave heights consistent with zero)

recipe.goal: Extract de-projected azimuthal, radial and vertical velocities versus radius
recipe.method: EDDY in concentric annuli using the Gaussian line centroid and the simple harmonic oscillator (SHO) method for 3D velocities
key_parameters: Annuli spaced by 20% of the beam size, oriented at the disc PA and inclination from the Keplerian fit
Fit restricted to position angles within 20 deg of the major axis
assumptions: Systemic velocity fixed to the value from the Keplerian fit (vertical/systemic degeneracy)

recipe.goal: Retrieve the gas radial density profile from the Keplerian deviations
recipe.method: Use the deviation of v_phi from Keplerian as a proxy for the radial pressure gradient, solve the midplane force balance for d ln(rho)/dr and integrate over r
key_parameters: beta=-0.14, T0=38 K, r0=73 au (from ARKS 13CO fit)
M_star = 1.91 Msun so that Keplerian speed at 75 au equals the measured azimuthal velocity
assumptions: Mean molecular weight mu = 14 (C and O dominated, secondary gas) or 2.3 (H2 dominated, primordial); midplane z=0; power-law temperature

recipe.goal: Validate the kinematic method with simulated Keplerian and pressure-supported observations
recipe.method: Synthetic 12CO cubes from DISC2RADMC, simulated ALMA observations with CASA simobserve, imaged with tclean, then processed like the data (velocity map, Keplerian residuals, azimuthal velocities)
key_parameters: Cubes with 26 m/s spectral resolution and 10 mas spatial resolution
Gaussian radial surface density centred at 74 au, FWHM 17 au, aspect ratio h=0.05, 1.91 Msun star
assumptions: LTE, kinetic and excitation temperature 38 K at the belt centre decaying with exponent -0.14; mu = 14 or 2.3; radial and vertical velocities zero
